title: Selvage Session Protocol — error codes and close codes
description: The machine-readable vocabulary of `selvage/1` faults: `error.code` on a response, `session.error.params.code` on an event, and the WebSocket close code that a fatal fault is paired with. Valid against PROTOCOL.md §11.

errorCode.description: Every code `selvage/1` defines. `doc_not_open` is reserved and never produced by this slice; a code a receiver does not know is treated as an unknown fault, not as a protocol error.

closeCode.description: WebSocket close codes, in the private-use range: 4000 protocol_error, 4001 room_unknown, 4002 token_invalid, 4003 room_gone, 4004 host_present, 4005 unsupported_version.

fatalCode.description: A code that closes the connection: `session.error` first, then a close carrying the matching code, so a client that does not read close frames still learns why.

closeForCode.description: The close code the server pairs with a fatal error code. The other codes leave the connection open.

errorObject.description: `error` on a response (§4.2) and `params` on a `session.error` event (§6) are the same shape. `message` is human-readable and explicitly not stable, so nothing may depend on it.
